messages:
alex: Quick sync — noticed an ingestion delta between token_cost_events and token_latency_events for the last 6h. token_cost is down ~28% but latency events count looks normal. Did something change in the router or schema?

riley: @alex thanks for flagging. Any chance you can share the query you used? Curious if this is a filtering issue on our side or upstream. :eyes:

alex: pasted query I ran against metrics-prod (single line):
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM token_cost_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours'
```
Also grabbed one raw event from the latency stream that correlates to a request we saw:
```json
{"ts": "2026-03-16T19:12:04Z", "request_id": "req_34f2", "model": "redwood-3b", "tokens": 142, "lat_ms": 78, "route": "/generate"}
```

samira: glancing quickly — we did a small router change yesterday to truncate metadata fields > 1KB to avoid large header errors with some customers. Could be we accidentally dropped an indexing field used by the cost pipeline. @matt any idea?

matt: Hmm — the cost pipeline relies on event.event_meta.model_variant and event.event_meta.token_weight. If the truncation removed event_meta, ingestion mapping will drop those rows from token_cost_events. I haven't seen alerts but could be subtle.

alex: OK that matches: the latency event above has no event_meta key. We used to have event_meta: {"model_variant":"rwd-3b-q4", "token_weight":1.0}.

riley: Confirming — token_cost_events has an early filter that ignores events without event_meta.token_weight (we added that to dedupe some malformed logs). If event_meta was stripped upstream, they won't be counted.

matt: I'll patch the ingestion lambda to fall back to parsing model and tokens from the top-level fields if event_meta is absent. Will also add a synthetic token_weight default of 1.0. Pushing a quick fix to staging now.

samira: Thank you. I'll revert the router truncation rule for metadata for the next canary, and add a guard so we only truncate very large single attributes rather than the whole object.

alex: Appreciate it. Two follow-ups: (1) can we add a small alert if token_cost_events drops >10% vs latency stream for 1h? (2) can we add a migration to backfill the last 12h if ingestion missed event_meta?

matt: (1) yes — I can add a k8s-alert in pager duty. (2) backfill is doable but will need a small mapping job to re-parse raw_event blob; estimate ~2-3h work and a short maintenance window to avoid double-counting.

riley: I'll own the alert once matt creates the rule. For the backfill, let's sync schedule with infra so we don't overload ES.

samira: I'll update the canary checklist to exclude metadata truncation flags and add a note to notify analytics when we touch router payload transformations.

alex: Sounds good. Next steps: matt pushes lambda fix -> staging test -> matt kicks off backfill (if staging looks clean) -> riley wires alert -> samira updates canary docs. Ping here when each step is done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
